boundary_rationale: The poem turns from catalog to hymn: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֔ב כִּסְאֲךָ֖ לְדֹ֥ר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier) reopens direct address to YHWH after the descriptive verses behind it, “You, Yahweh, remain forever. Your throne is from generation to generation.” (web:Lam.5.19). The petition, הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ ונשוב וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here, ketiv/qere ונשוב / וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה, both readings meaning turn or return), “Turn us to yourself, Yahweh, and we will be turned.” (web:Lam.5.21). Whether 5:19-5:22 forms a close of its own or reads on from the petition before it is held open rather than decided; the poem's closing word stays unresolved, “you have utterly rejected us” (web:Lam.5.22).
